prompts.display_text: Pin a country that borders Peru and has at least one dedicated temple (as of October 2026).
prompts.text_original: A country that shares a land border with Peru and has at least one dedicated temple (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology (dedicated, under construction, announced), read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Peru borders five countries, and every one of them has a dedicated temple: Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil, Bolivia and Chile. Peru itself has four dedicated temples, led by Lima (1986). Bolivia is the least obvious neighbour, with its one temple in Cochabamba.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: São Paulo Brazil Temple 1978 and eleven more.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country outside the US where a future President of the Church served as a missionary or led a mission.
prompts.text_original: A country outside today's United States where a President of the Church had served as a full-time missionary or presided over a mission before becoming Church President.
prompts.citation: Presidents of the Church Student Manual, chapters 2-9 and 13-15; Thomas S. Monson biography on churchofjesuschrist.org/learn, read 4 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Ten of the Church's presidents served in the British Isles before their calls, from Brigham Young in 1839 to Gordon B. Hinckley in the 1930s. Others went farther: Lorenzo Snow to Italy and Switzerland, John Taylor to France and Germany, Heber J. Grant to Japan, and Thomas S. Monson to Canada as a mission president. Joseph F. Smith also served in Hawaii, then an independent kingdom.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Brigham Young, John Taylor, Wilford Woodruff, Lorenzo Snow, Joseph F. Smith, Heber J. Grant, George Albert Smith, David O. McKay (Scotland), Ezra Taft Benson and Gordon B. Hinckley all served there.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: John Taylor's 1849-52 mission covered France and Germany.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: John Taylor (1849-52) and Lorenzo Snow taught there.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Lorenzo Snow opened the Italian Mission, 1849-52.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: Thomas S. Monson presided over the Canadian Mission in Toronto, 1959-62.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Lorenzo Snow directed missionary work in Switzerland during his Italian mission.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Heber J. Grant opened and presided over the Japanese Mission, 1901-03.

prompts.display_text: Pin a landlocked country (no sea coast) where the Church has at least one stake as of October 2026.
prompts.text_original: A landlocked country (no sea coast) where the Church has at least one stake as of October 2026.
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (figures of 31 Dec 2025), read 4 Nov 2026; Uganda stake from its Global Histories overview
prompts.summary: Twelve landlocked countries have stakes. Bolivia leads with 33, then Zimbabwe (12), Paraguay (11) and Switzerland (5). Austria, Mongolia, Malawi and Uganda have 2 or more; Hungary, the Czech Republic, Zambia and Botswana have one each. Landlocked Nepal, Laos, Ethiopia, Rwanda, Armenia and Slovakia have congregations but no stake yet.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where English is an official or de facto official language and the Church has over 50,000 members (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: A country where English is an official or de facto official language and the Church had more than 50,000 members at the end of 2025 (latest figures as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (membership, 31 Dec 2025); Wikipedia country infoboxes (official languages)
prompts.summary: English-speaking countries hold much of the Church's membership: the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand, plus the Philippines, Nigeria and Ghana. South Africa, Zimbabwe, Samoa and Tonga also list English among their official languages; each had over 50,000 members at the end of 2025. English is only de facto official in the UK and Australia. Papua New Guinea (46,583) falls short.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: English, Maori and NZ Sign Language; 120,992 members.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: English is one of 12 official languages; 78,689 members.

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: English is among 16 official languages; 52,430 members.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country that holds a place or a people named in the books of Ezra or Nehemiah.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country that holds a place or people named in Ezra or Nehemiah
prompts.note: Site is in the West Bank or Gaza; a player may reasonably pin ISR as well.
prompts.summary: Ezra and Nehemiah tell of exiles returning from Babylon to rebuild Jerusalem. Nehemiah left the Persian palace at Shushan, cedar came from Lebanon by way of Tyre and Sidon, and the builders were mocked by Sanballat of Samaria, Tobiah the Ammonite and Geshem the Arabian (Nehemiah 2:19).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Both books are about rebuilding Jerusalem's temple and walls (Ezra 1:3; Nehemiah 2:17).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: The exiles returned from Babylon under Cyrus's decree (Ezra 1:11).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Nehemiah was cupbearer at Shushan the palace when he heard of Jerusalem's ruin (Nehemiah 1:1).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Men of Jericho built part of the wall, and Sanballat mocked from Samaria (Nehemiah 3:2; 4:2).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: The Levites' prayer recalls the signs against Pharaoh in Egypt (Nehemiah 9:9).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Tobiah the Ammonite, an enemy of the wall, came from Ammon east of the Jordan (Nehemiah 2:10).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Cedar came by sea from Lebanon through Zidon and Tyre for the temple (Ezra 3:7).

answers.name: Saudi Arabia
answers.fact: Geshem the Arabian joined the scoffers against Nehemiah (Nehemiah 2:19).
